description: Period-level status joining what reporting was expected to any produced immutable revisions and delivery materializations. An obligation exists before its first revision or webhook, making missing-first-report detection possible. All nested revisions and materializations MUST match this obligation's authenticated caller/account, configuration generation, report definition, feed, period, and scope.

accepted_adjustment_receipt_count.description: Number of accepted adjustment receipts. Reconciled Billing buyers do not post an adjustment until their exact digest is accepted.

accepted_receipt_count.description: Number of accepted receipts. At most one current accepted receipt per consumer and revision contributes to reconciliation_status. Present iff reconciliation_mode is consumer_receipt.

adjustment_count.description: Number of immutable post-official reporting adjustment records for this obligation in the consistent ledger snapshot.

adjustment_receipt_count.description: Number of authenticated receipts for adjustments targeting this obligation's official revision. Reconciled Billing only.

consumer_status_count.description: Complete number of immutable authenticated consumer status statements associated with this obligation in the ledger snapshot, whether originally joined by reporting_obligation_id or by the exact configuration-generation, report-definition, and period key before the obligation existed. Core status-sync history is counted independently from Reconciled Billing receipts.

coverage.description: Immutable effective coverage of the exact selected offering at this period boundary. Delivery health is evaluated separately over the covered denominator.

limitations.description: Stable reasons that some requested scope is not covered by the exact selected offering. These are capability facts, not delivery failures.

media_buy_ids.description: Exact media-buy denominator, including unsupported and unknown buys. An empty array is an explicitly evaluated zero-buy scope.

package_ids.description: Exact package denominator for the evaluated media buys.

coverage.title: Reporting Coverage

x-adcp-validation.aggregation: Metrics computed only over covered_package_ids MUST be labeled partial whenever status is not full and MUST NOT be represented as complete media-buy or campaign totals. Implementations MUST NOT weaken the selected report definition to create an undeclared lowest-common-denominator profile.
x-adcp-validation.partition: The four media-buy classification arrays MUST be pairwise disjoint and their union MUST equal media_buy_ids. The three package classification arrays MUST be pairwise disjoint and their union MUST equal package_ids. Every limitation media_buy_id and package_id MUST belong to those denominators.
x-adcp-validation.status: full requires every media buy to be fully covered and every package covered; the explicit empty denominator is full. partial requires at least one covered package, fully covered media buy, or partially covered media buy and at least one partial, unsupported, or unknown item. A partially covered media buy counts as a covered item when excluding none and unknown. none requires a nonempty denominator, no covered item, at least one unsupported item, and no unknown item. unknown requires a nonempty denominator, no covered item, and at least one unknown item.

current_consumer_status_id.description: Current unsuperseded consumer status statement associated with this obligation by seller ID or its exact logical period key. Omitted when consumer_status_count is zero.

destination_ref.description: Immutable caller-owned destination generation selected by this account-authorized obligation. The account/configuration join—not possession of this reusable reference—authorizes disclosure. Present when and only when the obligation’s configuration selects a managed-delivery offering; Core (API-delivered) obligations omit every destination and materialization field.

items.description: Structured reporting condition that explains delayed or action_required health without exposing credentials, provider response bodies, or internal stack traces.

external_ref.description: Optional opaque, non-secret correlation string for the party's own tracker — a ticket key, incident ID, or case number. Untrusted display text only. The character class excludes whitespace and the solidus, so the value cannot express a URL or a sentence; receivers compare, store, and display it as inert text and never dereference, resolve, or execute it. It confers no authorization and MUST NOT be used to look up state across accounts or callers.

issue_id.description: Seller-issued stable identifier for this logical issue: re-emissions and later polls of the same unresolved condition reuse it, and resolution retires it, so consumers can project AdCP reporting issues into durable work items. A recurrence after resolution receives a new id.

message.description: Untrusted display text only. SDKs and agents dispatch exclusively on closed code/recommended_action values and never execute embedded links or instructions.

opened_at.description: When the seller first observed this logical condition, carried unchanged across every re-emission until the issue is retired. It anchors the escalation clock advertised as consumer_mismatch_escalation_seconds and lets a consumer age an issue without keeping its own first-seen table. Required when code is CONSUMER_STATUS_MISMATCH.

reporting_revision_id.description: Published revision this issue concerns. Required when code is REVISION_UNREADABLE.

reporting_status_id.description: Current authenticated consumer status statement that caused this mismatch.

items.title: Reporting Status Issue

x-adcp-validation.consumer_mismatch_escalation: A CONSUMER_STATUS_MISMATCH issue MUST carry opened_at and the reporting_status_id that caused it. When the seller advertises consumer_mismatch_escalation_seconds, an open or acknowledged issue still unresolved at opened_at plus that window MUST be emitted at severity action_required with a recommended_action in the contact_ family — contact_buyer, contact_seller, or contact_provider — naming the diagnosed responsible_party, and the seller MUST advertise operations_contact so the named party is reachable. wait_for_retry MUST NOT survive the escalation boundary: an unattended mismatch is an escalation, not a retry. This escalation takes precedence over the stale-received grace window in get-reporting-status-response.json: when the two windows overlap, the escalation boundary wins and the issue is action_required even if the grace window has not closed. An issue already retired under consumer_mismatch_lifecycle is not subject to this rule, because it is no longer in issues[].
x-adcp-validation.consumer_mismatch_lifecycle: resolved requires a superseding agreeing consumer statement or a seller projection that no longer conflicts. waived is terminal only when consumer and seller explicitly agree off-protocol to disregard the exact caller/account mismatch identified by issue_id, causing reporting_status_id, and diagnosed conflict; a seller MUST NOT act unilaterally. Waiver leaves the consumer statement unchanged and not seller evidence. The seller retains a private audit, retires the issue from issues[], and projects underlying seller health even while the immutable statement remains current and visible in consumer_statuses[]. A later statement or different conflict is evaluated independently and receives a new issue_id if conflicting. A health change fires the advertised reporting.status_changed recovery transition with issue_ids empty or absent; otherwise no health-transition notification is required and polling remains authoritative.
x-adcp-validation.issue_lifecycle: issue_id identifies one logical condition. opened_at is fixed at first emission and MUST NOT advance while the same issue_id is re-emitted, even across ledger snapshots, health transitions, or a severity change from delayed to action_required. issue_state, when supported, moves only forward through open, acknowledged, and then resolved or waived; a recurrence after retirement receives a new issue_id and a new opened_at. external_ref is inert correlation text with no protocol meaning; a seller MUST NOT reuse one external_ref across callers on a caller-scoped issue, because that would leak the blast radius of a seller-side incident between tenants.
x-adcp-validation.revision_unreadable: REVISION_UNREADABLE means the seller cannot currently serve or verify the content of a published revision that it still owes through exact reads within status_retention_days. Examples: the stored rows are missing, or they no longer reproduce row_count, control_totals, and revision_content_sha256. PRODUCTION_FAILED does not apply, because the revision was produced and published. The issue names one affected reporting_obligation_id and the reporting_revision_id. When one revision serves several of the caller's obligations, the seller emits one issue per obligation. An affected obligation is neither healthy nor complete while the issue is open. The issue is delayed with wait_for_retry while automatic repair is in progress, and action_required with contact_seller once the seller cannot restore the content automatically. While the issue is open, an exact read of the revision by a caller authorized for it MUST return SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE. It MUST NOT return REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND, and it MUST NOT return rows that fail the binding. Unauthorized callers still receive the nondisclosing REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND. The revision's metadata stays listed in the ledger. The issue is retired when exact reads again return content that matches the committed binding, or when the revision's status_retention_days window ends. A seller MUST NOT retire it by serving different content under the same reporting_revision_id. Because an official revision cannot be superseded, an obligation whose official revision is lost does not become complete.

materialization_count.description: Number of materialization records for this obligation's revisions in the consistent ledger snapshot. Present iff the obligation is managed-delivery (destination_ref present).

media_buy_ids.description: Exact frozen media-buy denominator resolved for this period, including buys with zero rows. An empty array is the definitive zero-buy set; omission is never used to mean all, empty, or unknown.

pending_adjustment_count.description: Number of applicable adjustments without an accepted receipt. Reconciled Billing complete/healthy requires zero.

production_status.description: Whether any revision has been produced for this obligation. published includes zero-row revisions.

receipt_count.description: Complete number of authenticated receipts associated with this obligation in the ledger snapshot. Present iff reconciliation_mode is consumer_receipt.

reconciliation_status.description: Consumer agreement state for the current required revision. A later superseding revision returns a receipt-required obligation to pending until that revision is accepted.

resource_retained_until.description: Minimum time through which at least one verified materialization for a completed obligation remains readable. Managed-delivery only; Core revisions are retained per status_retention_days and readable through the existing API transports.

revision_count.description: Number of revision records for this obligation in the consistent ledger snapshot.

ReportingScheduleAlignment.description: Calendar used to establish exact period boundaries. source_timezone is an explicit upstream reporting clock, such as an ad server network timezone, that may differ from the AdCP account timezone. The obligation echoes resolved timestamps and source timezone.
ReportingScheduleAlignment.title: Reporting Schedule Alignment

schedule.description: Resolved immutable schedule generation that created this obligation.

delivery_sla.description: Non-negative maximum time after period end before the required revision is due. PT0S means due at period close; expected_at equals the resolved period end plus this duration.

period_anchor.description: Required for billing_cycle alignment. This immutable instant anchors the recurring half-open billing periods so producer and consumer derive the same month, quarter, or other contractual cycle.

period_duration.description: Strictly positive ISO 8601 duration of each reporting period, such as PT15M, P1D, or P1M.

period_timezone.description: Required IANA timezone for source_timezone and billing_cycle calendar arithmetic. A numeric UTC offset is not sufficient because it does not define DST transitions.

schedule.title: Reporting Schedule

x-adcp-validation.iana_timezone: Every period_timezone and echoed period.source_timezone value MUST be a recognized IANA Time Zone Database zone name or link, including UTC. Reject unknown identifiers before accepting a configuration; do not silently substitute the host timezone or a numeric offset.
x-adcp-validation.period_generation: Producer and consumer MUST derive the same ordered half-open intervals from period_duration, alignment, period_anchor, and period_timezone when applicable. utc alignment uses 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z as interval zero. account_timezone uses local midnight on that date in the account's resolved IANA timezone. source_timezone uses local midnight on that date in the explicit period_timezone. billing_cycle uses its explicit period_anchor expressed in period_timezone. Every boundary is calculated directly from that origin and the interval ordinal by multiplying each ISO 8601 duration component by the ordinal and applying years, months, days, hours, minutes, then seconds. Calendar durations use local civil-time arithmetic in the selected IANA timezone, including DST transitions; they are not converted to fixed seconds. Month/year addition preserves the origin's local day and time, clamping to the target month's final valid day when necessary. A nonexistent local boundary advances by the timezone gap; an ambiguous local boundary uses the earlier offset. Thus a clamped February boundary does not shift a March 31 anchor.
x-adcp-validation.source_compatibility: Before accepting a configuration, the seller MUST prove that its upstream source can produce every configured half-open period exactly, either natively or by lossless re-bucketing from finer-grained source data. source_timezone MUST equal the upstream reporting calendar used by the pinned report definition. A structural incompatibility MUST fail configuration validation and MUST NOT be represented as indefinitely waiting reporting. If incompatibility is discovered after acceptance, the configuration becomes action_required with the seller responsible.

scope_resolved_at.description: Instant at which the configured scope was resolved and frozen for this obligation. For all_media_buys, include every caller-authorized account media buy whose effective flight overlaps the half-open period and was known by this cutoff. Later-created or backdated buys do not rewrite this obligation.

successful_materialization_count.description: Number of available/delivered verified materializations in the consistent ledger snapshot. Present iff the obligation is managed-delivery (destination_ref present).

title: Reporting Obligation

x-adcp-validation.adjustment_reconciliation: For reconciliation_mode consumer_receipt, every adjustment is pending until the authenticated consumer records an accepted adjustment receipt with the exact canonical digest. A rejected receipt preserves the dispute and MUST NOT be represented as accepted settlement.
x-adcp-validation.complete_finality: complete requires a published revision at required_finality. For Core, that revision MUST remain readable through the exact revision-content binding declared by the seller for status_retention_days. Managed-delivery additionally requires at least one verified readable materialization for that revision through resource_retained_until. consumer_receipt additionally requires an accepted matching receipt for the current revision and an accepted receipt for every applicable adjustment; rejected adjustment evidence preserves a dispute and cannot be complete. A snapshot-required pacing obligation may therefore become complete from a snapshot revision.
x-adcp-validation.consumer_mismatch: Consumer status is separately attributed and never satisfies production or billing reconciliation. A current statement that conflicts with the seller's otherwise healthy/complete projection degrades only this authenticated caller/account view with a CONSUMER_STATUS_MISMATCH issue carrying opened_at and the causing reporting_status_id. Conflicts are obligation_missing, revision_missing, unreadable, content_mismatch, and received naming a revision that is no longer the current required revision after a seller restatement. Every conflict except that last one is immediately action_required. A received statement made stale only by a seller restatement is delayed until the grace deadline defined by get-reporting-status-response.json stale_received_grace — the first superseding revision's created_at plus the configuration generation's schedule.delivery_sla, or automated_recovery_window_seconds when that SLA resolves to zero — and action_required at or after it, because the buyer consumed exactly what the seller then required and has not yet had a bounded chance to re-read. Later restatements do not restart that window, and an advertised consumer_mismatch_escalation_seconds boundary takes precedence over it. The issue keeps one issue_id and one opened_at across that severity change, and is retired only under reporting-status-issue.json consumer_mismatch_lifecycle. An exact bilateral waiver retires the issue and restores this obligation's underlying seller health even while current_consumer_status_id continues to name the immutable causing statement; a later statement or materially different conflict is evaluated independently. The seller assigns responsible_party from the diagnosed cause; an uncorroborated consumer statement or waiver never changes another caller's view or seller-advertised reliability_statistics. Absence of consumer status is never a conflict: after expected_at plus automated_recovery_window_seconds it is counted in the response's obligation_counts.consumer_status_pending and changes no health.
x-adcp-validation.core_readability: For a Core (API-delivered) obligation — no destination_ref — healthy and complete assert an authoritative readable revision: production_status published, at least one immutable revision retained per status_retention_days, and readable through the existing get_media_buy_delivery and reporting_webhook transports. An open REVISION_UNREADABLE issue for any revision of the obligation also blocks healthy and complete. Managed-delivery obligations additionally require at least one successful retained materialization.
x-adcp-validation.coverage_resolution: coverage.evaluated_at MUST equal scope_resolved_at and coverage.media_buy_ids MUST equal media_buy_ids. A configuration requiring full coverage makes incomplete coverage action_required with REPORTING_COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE. allow_partial evaluates delivery health over covered_package_ids but never changes coverage.status or represents covered-subset aggregates as whole-scope totals.
x-adcp-validation.nested_identity: Every materialization associated with this obligation MUST equal its delivery_config_id, delivery_config_version, destination_ref, feed_purpose, and method; its destination-independent revision MUST equal account_id, report_definition_id, reporting_profile, period, and applicable media_buy_ids.
x-adcp-validation.obligation_availability: For every eligible elapsed period, the seller MUST commit the obligation independently of source availability and before committing any revision for that obligation or taking any get_reporting_status ledger snapshot whose ledger_as_of is later than period.end. A periods view whose selected denominator includes that configuration generation and period MUST include the obligation in its paginated record set. The seller MAY derive future boundaries and next_expected_at before close, but MUST NOT expose an obligation in a ledger snapshot whose ledger_as_of is at or before period.end or freeze an all_media_buys denominator before period.end. Media-buy acceptance alone does not create an obligation: the applicable reporting configuration generation determines the schedule, scope, finality, and delivery contract. Revision production, materialization, and any webhook MUST NOT be prerequisites for obligation creation.
x-adcp-validation.record_counts: revision_count is the number of distinct revision records for this obligation in ledger_snapshot_id. Reliable Reporting 1.0 requires adjustment_count. A seller advertising consumer_status_task additionally requires consumer_status_count; both fields remain schema-optional so readers can accept the published RC.1 shape. adjustment_count counts distinct adjustments targeting an official revision used by this obligation; one destination-independent adjustment is counted once even when it fans out through multiple materializations. consumer_status_count counts the authenticated caller's immutable status history associated either by reporting_obligation_id or by the exact delivery_config_id, delivery_config_version, report_definition_id, and period logical key. If the seller creates an obligation after receiving obligation_missing, the existing chain attaches to the repaired obligation by that logical key; it MUST NOT be lost, forked, or reset. current_consumer_status_id names the chain's one unsuperseded leaf. materialization_count, successful_materialization_count, receipt_count, accepted_receipt_count, adjustment_receipt_count, accepted_adjustment_receipt_count, and pending_adjustment_count, when present for their respective tiers, MUST equal the complete associated record totals in the same snapshot, even when records appear on different pages.
x-adcp-validation.revision_chain: Supersession MUST be acyclic, remain within this logical slice, and every supersedes_reporting_revision_id MUST name the immediately prior retained snapshot revision. At most one official revision may exist for a logical slice; it is terminal, and every obligation using that slice shares the same close. Later corrections are reporting adjustments and never alter this chain.
x-adcp-validation.scope_resolution: scope_resolved_at MUST equal period.end. all_media_buys membership is frozen from the caller-authorized AdCP media buys known at that instant whose effective flights overlap [period.start, period.end); explicit configured media_buy_ids are echoed even when they produce zero rows. Provider object deletion does not remove a buy. Later-created or backdated buys do not alter the obligation.
